translations.h1: Startup Recognition Support: DPIIT and Haryana
translations.short_description: Understand current startup-recognition criteria and separate central, state and tax routes. Rapid supports evidence, narrative and query-response preparation.
translations.intro_html:
Make your startup-recognition application explain the business clearly. Rapid helps organise the enterprise records, innovation narrative and supporting evidence, then supports preparation and factual query responses.

For a founder, the useful question is which recognition route fits the business and what it can support. Central DPIIT recognition, a Haryana registration and a separate benefit application should be planned as distinct steps.

sections.title: What is DPIIT startup recognition?
sections.html:
DPIIT recognition identifies an eligible startup under the central framework. It is not the same as incorporating a company. The official Startup India page directs recognition applications through the National Single Window System and sets out eligibility. DPIIT recognition.

An application should explain the actual innovation or improvement, business potential and supporting evidence. A recently incorporated entity is not automatically recognised.

sections.title: What do the current criteria say?
sections.html:
The official page reflects the February 2026 revision:

Criterion Published position
Entity Private company, registered partnership, LLP or cooperative society.
Age Up to 10 years; up to 20 for the DeepTech category.
Turnover Below ₹200 crore; ₹300 crore for DeepTech, under the stated criteria.
Business Innovation/improvement and employment or wealth-creation potential; not splitting/reconstruction of an existing business.

DeepTech status has its own evidence requirements; it is not a label a founder should assume from working with technology. Official recognition application and criteria.

sections.title: Recognition, tax benefits and funding are different
sections.nav_label: Recognition, tax benefits and funding are different
sections.html:
Objective What to examine
DPIIT recognition Central eligibility and application evidence.
Haryana startup registration or support Current state route and its separate conditions.
Tax relief The specific tax provision and separate eligibility/application.
Grant, investment or loan The programme or provider's own selection and terms.

Recognition does not automatically award funding or a tax exemption. Startup India presents recognition and the 80-IAC process separately. State-specific eligibility must be checked for the named programme rather than inferred from the central certificate.

items.title: A clear business explanation
items.html: Describe the problem, solution and what is different or improved. A manufacturing innovation can be explained through process or product evidence without exaggerated technology claims.

items.title: Evidence behind the narrative
items.html: Connect the application with product material, demonstrations, customer validation or other available records. Distinguish completed progress from future plans.

items.title: A practical next-step plan
items.html: Identify what you want recognition to support and which separate application comes next. This keeps expectations and effort aligned.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid reviews the proposed recognition route, organises the document checklist and helps structure the factual business narrative. We prepare supporting material and factual query responses while the founder confirms its accuracy. The applicant submits through their own official account; Rapid does not act as a DPIIT-appointed registration agent.

The company owns its claims and documents. DPIIT or the relevant state body makes the recognition decision. Tax opinions and formal certifications remain with the responsible professionals.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.html: Bring incorporation/registration records, ownership and authorised-contact details, a concise business explanation, product/process evidence, available turnover information and any earlier application. For an existing business, explain its history and relationship with other entities clearly.

items.title: 1. Identify the route and eligibility questions
items.html: Review the entity, age, activity and recognition objective.

items.title: 2. Organise evidence and narrative
items.html: Rapid helps make the business explanation understandable and supported by the records available.

items.title: 3. Support the applicant's submission and queries
items.html: The applicant makes the official submission. Rapid helps organise supporting records and factual responses to queries.

items.title: 4. Identify separate benefit applications
items.html: After the recognition decision, examine any tax, state-support or funding requirement on its own terms.

sections.title: Cost and timing

Time depends on evidence readiness and the reviewing body's process; a fixed recognition date or funding result is not promised.

items.title: Is a new company enough to qualify?
items.html: No. It must meet the recognition criteria, including the business-related requirements.

items.title: Can an established business apply?

Start before a shipment depends on a missing or outdated record. If you already hold an IEC, the work may concern an update or correction rather than a new code.

sections.title: What is an IEC?
sections.html:
The Importer Exporter Code is administered by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT). It identifies the entity for the applicable foreign-trade requirements. The code should be distinguished from a product permission, customs clearance or a foreign buyer's approval.

DGFT's current user manual explains the application process, bank details, supporting documents and payment. Official IEC manual.

sections.title: New application, update or product permission?

New IEC Entity and bank information for the code application.
Existing IEC with changed details Correcting or updating the registered information.
Annual confirmation/update Keeping the IEC record current under DGFT requirements.
Restricted or regulated goods Separate product or trade permissions, where applicable.

If your plan involves food, examine the FSSAI requirement alongside IEC. A code alone does not make every food import permissible.

sections.title: Why organise the record before the transaction?

items.title: Keep the trading entity consistent
items.html: The contract, invoice, bank account and application should identify the intended business correctly. Resolve differences in names or constitution before relying on the code.

items.title: Avoid unnecessary duplicate work
items.html: Check for an existing IEC and its status before treating the enquiry as a first application.

items.title: Identify the other shipment requirements

sections.title: What is FSSAI registration or licensing?
sections.html:
FSSAI regulates food businesses through registration and licensing under the food-safety framework. Applications are handled through FoSCoS, with the applicable route determined by the business category and current criteria. Official application portal.

The requirement concerns the food-business activity. It does not replace land-use permission, building approval or pollution consent where those apply.

sections.title: Registration, State licence or Central licence?
sections.html:
The turnover thresholds changed from 1 April 2026:

General turnover band Published route
Up to ₹1.5 crore Registration.
Above ₹1.5 crore and up to ₹50 crore State licence.
Above ₹50 crore Central licence.

These replace the older turnover bands. FSSAI order dated 13 March 2026.

The kind of business still matters. The revised eligibility table separately lists categories such as importers with Central licensing irrespective of turnover. Use the current category table for your activity rather than applying the general bands blindly. FoSCoS eligibility and fee table.

items.title: The food activity and products
items.html: A mill, oil processor, cold store and importer perform different activities. List what the premises actually does and the products involved.

items.title: The premises and operating arrangement
items.html: Identify who runs the business, whether the premises is owned or leased, and what other activities happen there. A brand owner and a manufacturer may have different responsibilities.

items.title: The food-safety preparation
items.html: Bring the hygiene, layout, water and process information required for the particular application. The evidence should describe working arrangements at the premises.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid identifies the application category with your team, prepares the document checklist and coordinates the business and premises records. We follow the agreed application and help organise responses to queries or observations.

The food-business operator confirms the information and maintains food-safety practices. Testing and professional reports come from the responsible providers. FSSAI or the designated licensing authority makes the registration/licensing decision.

sections.title: Fees, validity and timing

Confirm the current payment requirements for the selected service on the portal. Rapid's fee, testing and premises improvements are separate.

The 2026 reform introduces perpetual validity subject to the applicable framework and risk-based inspections. This does not remove food-safety duties or the need to keep material particulars current. Existing-record transition and payment requirements should be checked on FoSCoS. FSSAI reform notice.

Preparation and any inspection/query process affect the timeline. Do not rely on a universal same-day licence promise for every food-business category.

sections.title: What is an LEI?
sections.html:
A Legal Entity Identifier is a 20-character identifier linked to reference information about a legal entity. It helps identify counterparties in financial transactions. LEIs are issued through the recognised issuing organisations in the global system, not by a consultancy simply creating a number. GLEIF: obtaining an LEI.

A requirement to hold an LEI depends on the applicable transaction or regulatory rule. Ask the requesting bank to identify the entity and requirement instead of assuming every business needs one for every loan.

sections.title: New registration, renewal or transfer?
sections.html:
Situation Work to consider
Entity has no LEI New registration through an eligible issuer.
Existing record is due for renewal Validate and update the reference information.
Name or corporate details changed Modification with supporting evidence.
Moving to another issuer Transfer of the existing LEI, not creation of a second identity.

Check for an existing code before applying. GLEIF's system supports public verification of entity information and status.

items.title: Match the bank's counterparty
items.html: The borrowing or transacting entity may differ from a group company or trading name. Resolve that distinction before submitting the application.

items.title: Keep the status usable
items.html: Issuance is not the only action. Timely renewal and updates keep reference information current for the processes that rely on it.

items.title: Avoid contradictory corporate records
items.html: Name changes, legal form and ownership information should be supported by the right documents rather than informal explanations.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid prepares a document checklist, helps reconcile the legal-entity information and coordinates the agreed application or renewal. We track issuer queries and help organise the applicant's responses.

items.title: 4. Retain the code and next renewal date

Rapid's coordination fee is separate. Timing depends on document consistency, issuer validation and responses to queries. A bank's transaction deadline does not guarantee an issuer will complete validation by that date.

sections.title: What is Udyam registration?
sections.html:
Udyam is the Ministry of MSME's national registration system. Registration is free, online and based on self-declaration; the official system issues a permanent registration number and certificate. It does not require renewal. The Ministry directs applicants to its official portal and government facilitation channels. Official Udyam guidance.

Use the government Udyam portal for registration. Rapid is not the government portal and does not present this service as a paid substitute for the official process.

sections.title: Which MSME category applies?
sections.html:
The revised classification effective 1 April 2025 uses investment in plant and machinery/equipment and turnover together:

Category Investment ceiling Turnover ceiling
Micro ₹2.5 crore ₹10 crore
Small ₹25 crore ₹100 crore
Medium ₹125 crore ₹500 crore

Both criteria apply. Use the official rules for the calculation and classification, rather than comparing a total project budget with one column. Ministry classification table.

items.title: A recognised enterprise record
items.html: Keep the enterprise identity available for the business processes that request it. Ensure the entity in a project application is the same one shown in the relevant records.

items.title: A starting point for programme checks
items.html: A scheme or lending product may refer to MSME status. That makes the registration relevant, while the particular programme still has its own conditions.

items.title: Clearer planning as the business grows
items.html: A larger investment or changing turnover can affect classification. Keep the enterprise record connected to current financial information rather than relying on an old category label.

sections.title: What Udyam does not replace
sections.html:
Requirement Why it remains separate
Site and operating permissions Registration does not authorise every activity at every location.
Loan sanction A lender assesses repayment capacity and its product conditions.
Subsidy approval The programme determines eligible applicant, expenditure and dates.
HUM Haryana's state enterprise record has a different purpose.

See HUM guidance, Subsidies and Incentives and Finance for those next questions.

sections.title: What Rapid's guidance covers
sections.html:
We help identify how the enterprise's registration and project facts connect to a wider advisory requirement. For example, a machinery-expansion discussion needs to distinguish the registered enterprise from the new asset expenditure and production dates.

The official portal and government facilitation system remain the registration route. Any Rapid engagement concerns the separately agreed project or advisory work, with a stated fee and deliverable.

sections.title: Information for a useful discussion

Bring the existing certificate if available, the enterprise name and activity, the specific scheme or finance question, proposed investment details and the request that prompted the registration enquiry. Your CA can help explain financial figures and classification inputs.

There is no need to submit Aadhaar numbers, passwords or OTPs in the public enquiry form.

items.html: The classification refers to the prescribed plant/machinery or equipment measure. Use the official calculation rules and your financial records.

sections.title: What does industrial insurance mean?
sections.html:
Industrial insurance is a broad description of cover for business assets and related risks. The relevant products can address property damage, machinery, goods movement or liability, with separate terms and exclusions. It is not one universal policy covering every loss.

IRDAI's consumer information explains the range of general-insurance cover and the importance of appropriate asset values. The actual policy wording, schedule and endorsements determine a particular contract. IRDAI general-insurance guidance.

sections.title: What does claim-management support involve?
sections.html:
Claim support brings the policy, incident and loss evidence into a clear record. It helps the policyholder respond to requests and track outstanding actions. It does not replace the insurer's decision or the role of an appointed surveyor/loss assessor.

The policy wording and circumstances determine the claim. A loss amount requested by the business, an assessed amount and a settlement offer are different figures.

sections.title: What should happen after a loss?

Priority Practical action
Safety and loss containment Use the responsible emergency and technical teams.
Insurer notification Follow the policy's reporting process and retain acknowledgement.
Evidence Keep photographs, incident details and relevant records where safe.
Survey and document requests Maintain a list of requested, supplied and outstanding items.
Repairs or disposal Coordinate with the insurer/surveyor's requirements before evidence is lost.

The exact process depends on the policy and incident. IRDAI's general-insurance material explains claims and the role of salvage; the policy and insurer's instructions remain the specific reference. IRDAI non-life guidance.

items.title: One reliable incident record
items.html: Bring the date, location, sequence and affected assets together. Avoid different versions of the incident being sent from different departments.

items.title: Evidence behind the loss calculation
items.html: Connect the claimed items with invoices, stock records, repair estimates and other relevant support. Identify estimates as estimates.

items.title: Clear follow-up ownership
items.html: Track who is supplying the next document and what the insurer is awaiting. This makes delays easier to address than an informal chain of calls.

sections.title: What does land-planning advisory cover?
sections.html:
The work examines the relationship between a parcel and a proposed use. It can include an initial planning review, coordination of site information and comparison of development assumptions. It does not replace a legal title opinion, certified valuation or detailed engineering design.

Haryana's TCP Department publishes development plans, controlled-area information and policies. These are starting records for the site-specific planning review. Official planning records.

sections.html:

Buy or reject a site Intended use, access, records and unresolved constraints.
Develop, lease or retain land Cost, timing, income assumptions and management commitment.
Choose between factory, warehouse or commercial use Applicable planning route and the demands of each model.
Phase a larger parcel Infrastructure needs, cash commitments and delivery sequence.

An indicative option is not an approved entitlement. Keep market assumptions separate from verified planning facts.

sections.title: What a useful review brings into focus

items.title: The buildable and usable proposition
items.html: Gross area alone does not explain the development. Access, site shape, levels, common works and planning controls can affect the usable proposal.

items.title: The real cost of the option

items.title: The next decision and its evidence

sections.title: What are balance transfer and top-up?
sections.html:
A balance transfer refinances an existing loan with another lender. A top-up adds borrowing for a permitted purpose. They can be considered together, but approval of one does not automatically approve the other.

If you want the existing lender to revise your rate without transferring the loan, see Interest-Rate Reduction.

translations.intro_html:

Start with what the money will do: buy equipment, support stock or fund a new facility. The appropriate credit structure follows the need and the lender's assessment.

sections.title: What does collateral-free mean?
sections.html:
Collateral-free lending generally concerns the absence of additional collateral under the relevant product or scheme. It does not mean interest-free funding, no repayment obligation or no assessment of the business.

CGTMSE distinguishes primary security in the business/financed assets from additional collateral and explains the treatment of guarantees. The proposed sanction should state the actual obligations. CGTMSE security guidance.

sections.title: How does CGTMSE fit?
sections.html:
CGTMSE provides guarantee cover to eligible lending institutions for qualifying credit to micro and small enterprises. It is not a direct loan application to the Trust. The published framework supports eligible credit up to ₹10 crore from 1 April 2025, subject to its conditions. Ministry overview.

A scheme ceiling is not an amount every applicant can borrow. The lender must approve the credit case. CGTMSE also describes a hybrid-security option, so the exact covered and secured portions should be understood. Credit-facility parameters.

items.title: A specific funding purpose
items.html: Show the cost and business role of the equipment, stock or project being financed. A round-number request without a use-of-funds explanation is difficult to evaluate.

items.title: A credible repayment basis
items.html: Connect projected sales, margins and collection times with the repayment schedule. New businesses should identify assumptions; operating businesses should reconcile forecasts with their records.

items.title: A clear view of existing obligations
items.html: Include current loans and other commitments. A financing proposal needs to show the complete repayment burden.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid prepares the funding brief, coordinates the document set and helps structure the business and cash-flow explanation. We support the agreed lender approach, track queries and organise the outstanding sanction or disbursement inputs.

The lender decides eligibility, security, pricing and amount. Rapid is neither the lender nor the guarantor and does not promise approval because Udyam or a guarantee scheme is available.

sections.html:
Bring Why it matters
Entity, activity and registration records Identifies the borrower.
Financial statements, tax records and bank statements Shows performance and cash movement.
Existing loans and repayment history Establishes current obligations.
Quotations or use-of-funds breakdown Supports the requested amount.
Cash-flow assumptions and own contribution Explains how the requirement will be funded and repaid.

items.title: 2. Prepare the business case

items.html: Organise the agreed submission and responses to credit questions.

items.title: 4. Review the offer and outstanding conditions
items.html: Help make the repayment, charges and obligations visible before you accept the facility.

sections.html:
Separate interest, lender processing charges, any applicable guarantee fee, professional costs and Rapid's fee. “Collateral-free” does not mean cost-free. A guarantee mechanism also does not remove lender scrutiny or document requirements.

Timing depends on the borrower, facility and credit assessment. We define the preparation work after reviewing your available records.

items.title: Can a new business be considered?
items.html: It can be examined under the relevant product, but projections and promoter capability need a credible basis.

items.title: Do I apply directly to CGTMSE for money?
items.html: The credit application is considered by the lending institution; guarantee cover follows its applicable process.

items.title: Does collateral-free mean no personal obligations?
items.html: Read the proposed sanction and relevant scheme conditions. Do not infer every obligation from the product label.

items.title: Will a higher scheme ceiling increase my eligible amount?
items.html: The lender still determines the amount justified by the business and its credit policy.

translations.h1: Working Capital Finance Support
translations.short_description: Plan cash-credit, overdraft or operating-finance requirements around stock and receivables. Rapid supports lender applications and facility reviews.
translations.intro_html:
Keep your funding aligned with the way money moves through the business. Rapid helps you explain the gap between paying for stock and collecting from customers, choose the facility to examine and coordinate the agreed lender application.

For a mill buying seasonal raw material, a manufacturer waiting on customer payments or a distributor building stock, the right discussion starts with the operating cycle rather than a round-number loan request.

sections.title: What is working capital finance?
sections.html:
Working capital supports operating needs such as inventory, production and receivables. It differs from long-term funding for a building or machine. Banks offer structures including cash credit, overdrafts, demand loans and bill-based facilities, depending on the business and product. SBI working-capital explanation.

This is a description of facility types, not a recommendation of one lender or a promise of its terms.

sections.title: Which facility should be examined?
sections.html:
Need Type of discussion
Recurring stock and receivables gap Cash-credit or overdraft structure.
A defined seasonal requirement Time-bound operating finance.
Documented sales awaiting payment Bill/invoice financing where suitable.
A long-lived machine or building Equipment or project finance, rather than consuming operating liquidity.

The lender determines the available product, eligible assets and limits. A sanction amount and the amount currently drawable can differ under the facility's conditions.

sections.title: What makes the funding calculation useful?

items.title: Map the cash cycle
items.html: Show how long stock is held, when suppliers are paid and when customers pay. The funding gap sits between those events.

items.title: Make seasonality visible
items.html: A grain processor's peak stock requirement may differ sharply from an average month. Explain the peak and how the borrowing reduces after collections.

items.title: Reconcile records with the request
items.html: Stock statements, debtor ageing, turnover and bank movements should tell a consistent story. Identify slow-moving inventory and overdue receivables rather than treating them as immediately collectible cash.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid prepares the funding brief and document checklist, coordinates the operating and financial evidence and supports the agreed lender application. We follow up on questions and help make reporting, renewal and sanction conditions visible to your finance team.

Management owns forecasts and stock/debtor declarations. The lender assesses limits, drawing conditions, security and price. Rapid does not certify inventory or guarantee customer collections.

sections.title: Documents to bring
sections.html:
Bring Why it matters
Financial statements and tax records Establishes the operating history.
Bank statements and existing facilities Shows cash movement and current borrowing.
Stock, receivables and creditor ageing Explains funds tied up in the cycle.
Monthly sales and purchase pattern Identifies seasonality and peak demand.
Forecast, orders and customer terms Supports the proposed requirement.
Current sanction and reporting conditions Shows what a renewal or enhancement must address.

items.title: 1. Understand the operating gap
items.html: Rapid reviews the timing of purchases, production and collections.

items.title: 2. Prepare the facility case
items.html: Coordinate the records and explain the amount and period of funding required.

items.title: 3. Support the lender discussion
items.html: Organise the authorised application and responses to the credit assessment.

items.title: 4. Track conditions and review dates
items.html: Help the team identify the documents and ongoing reporting required by the agreed facility.

sections.title: Costs, renewal and timing
sections.html:
Compare interest on the relevant utilisation basis, processing/renewal charges and other applicable costs. The sanction should explain reporting, drawing-power and review requirements. Rapid's fee is separate.

An enhancement or renewal can require updated performance and stock/debtor records. Start before a review date becomes an urgent operating problem. The lender controls approval and availability of funds.

items.title: Is the sanctioned limit always available to draw?
items.html: The facility's drawing-power and other conditions can limit current availability.

items.title: Can I use working capital to buy a building?
items.html: The permitted end use governs the facility. Discuss a suitable long-term structure instead of assuming operating finance can fund it.

items.title: Can a seasonal business be considered?
items.html: Yes, the application should explain its seasonal peak and repayment cycle; the lender decides suitability.

items.title: Will higher turnover automatically increase the limit?
items.html: The lender assesses the complete requirement and credit position, not one figure alone.

sections.title: Discuss your requirement
sections.html:
Tell us your activity, monthly or seasonal funding gap and current facility. An expert consultant from Rapid will call you to understand the requirement and explain the proposed work, fee and next steps.

translations.title: Business Loan Interest-Rate Reduction
translations.h1: Business Loan Interest-Rate Reduction
translations.short_description: Review repricing of an existing business loan. Rapid coordinates current terms, a supported lender request and the net effect of any revised offer.
translations.intro_html:
Review whether your existing business loan can be repriced on a better basis. Rapid helps you understand the current interest terms, prepare a documented request and coordinate the agreed discussion with your lender.

The objective is a lower borrowing cost where the evidence and lender terms support it. Start with the current facility before assuming that moving the entire loan is the only option.

sections.title: What does interest-rate reduction involve?
sections.html:
Interest-rate reduction means seeking a revision to the pricing of an existing loan. It can involve understanding the benchmark, the spread charged above it, reset terms and the lender's repricing policy.

This service was previously labelled “ROI Deduction”. Here ROI means rate of interest. It is not a tax-deduction service or a guarantee of improved investment returns.

sections.title: Repricing, reset or balance transfer?
sections.html:
Situation What to examine
Benchmark-linked rate changes Contractual reset timing and how the applicable benchmark is reflected.
Request for a lower spread or revised pricing The lender's review/conversion process and supporting credit case.
Alternative lender offers better terms Full balance-transfer comparison, including costs.
Need for additional borrowing A separate top-up or facility assessment.

A lower rate offered to a new borrower does not establish that the same price automatically applies to an existing contract.

sections.title: What a useful rate review should show

items.title: The actual current pricing
items.html: Bring the sanction, latest statement and rate-change communications together. Identify whether the facility is fixed or floating and what the contract says about resets.

items.title: The net benefit after charges
items.html: A conversion or repricing fee can reduce the benefit. Compare the remaining repayment cash flows, not just the first month's interest difference.

items.title: The credit case for the request
items.html: Updated performance and repayment conduct may help explain the request. The lender decides how these affect its pricing; improved numbers are not an automatic entitlement to a quoted reduction.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid prepares a current-terms summary, coordinates the records for the repricing request and compares any written proposal against the existing arrangement. We follow up on the agreed lender discussion and help you understand the change before accepting it.

The borrower authorises the request. The lender decides the revised rate, conditions and effective date. Rapid does not amend the loan agreement or promise a percentage reduction on the lender's behalf.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.html:
Bring Why it matters
Sanction and loan agreement Establishes benchmark, spread and contractual terms.
Latest statement and repayment schedule Shows balance and remaining cost.
Recent rate/reset communications Explains how current pricing was reached.
Updated financials and repayment record Supports the business case for review.
Alternative offer, if any Provides a documented comparison.
Proposed conversion/repricing charge Allows a net-benefit calculation.

For applicable loans, use the lender's Key Facts Statement to compare the important cost information. RBI KFS explanation.

items.title: 1. Establish the existing terms
items.html: Rapid reviews the facility records and the outcome you want.

items.title: 2. Prepare a supported request
items.html: Coordinate the updated business evidence and identify the specific pricing change being sought.

items.title: 3. Follow the lender's response
items.html: Track the agreed discussion and obtain the proposed terms in writing.

items.title: 4. Compare and confirm the effect
items.html: Show the rate, effective date, fees and repayment effect so you can decide whether to accept. Keep the lender's final confirmation with the loan records.

sections.title: Fees, savings and timing
sections.html:
Rapid's fee and any lender conversion charge are separate. A projected saving depends on the outstanding balance, future rates, repayment pattern and remaining term. State those assumptions rather than presenting an estimate as money already saved.

The lender's review process controls the decision and date. If repricing is unsuitable, a transfer can be examined separately without treating it as an automatic next action.

items.title: Will an RBI rate cut immediately reduce my instalment?
items.html: It depends on the facility's benchmark, reset and contractual terms. Review the actual agreement and lender communication.

items.title: Can I keep the same lender?
items.html: Yes, this service starts with reviewing repricing of the existing facility.

items.title: Is the lowest rate always the best option?
items.html: Compare charges, tenure and other conditions as well as the rate.

items.title: Can you guarantee a reduction?
items.html: No. Rapid prepares and coordinates the request; the lender controls the outcome.

sections.html:
Share the loan type, outstanding amount, current rate and remaining term. An expert consultant from Rapid will call you to understand the requirement and explain the proposed work, fee and next steps.

translations.title: Main Board & SME IPO Advisory
translations.h1: Main Board and SME IPO Readiness Advisory
translations.short_description: Prepare corporate, financial and business records for a potential IPO. Rapid coordinates readiness work with your appointed professionals.
translations.intro_html:
Prepare your company for a serious listing discussion. Rapid helps promoters organise business, financial and corporate records, identify readiness work and coordinate with the professionals responsible for a potential Main Board or SME issue.

Start with what the capital will achieve and whether the business is ready for the obligations of a listed company. The right first step may be preparation rather than choosing an exchange immediately.

sections.title: What does IPO readiness mean?
sections.html:
Readiness concerns the company's ability to support due diligence, explain its business and use of funds, and meet the governance and reporting demands of the intended route. It is different from issue approval or a promise that investors will subscribe.

The exchange and current regulatory framework determine the route's requirements. NSE identifies merchant bankers and other intermediaries in its SME issue process. NSE EMERGE overview.

sections.title: Main Board or SME: what should be compared?
sections.html:
Decision area Question for the company and appointed intermediary
Eligibility Does the company meet the current route-specific criteria?
Capital objective What funds are required and how will they be used?
Governance and reporting Can the organisation sustain the required responsibilities?
Issue costs and readiness effort What preparation and transaction costs need budgeting?
Timing Which records, restructuring or approvals must precede the issue?

A smaller issue does not make the SME route free of ongoing obligations. Current quantitative eligibility should be established with the appointed issue professionals rather than inferred from a generic comparison.

items.title: A credible use-of-funds explanation
items.html: Connect growth plans with specific expenditure and business assumptions.

items.title: A usable due-diligence record
items.html: Organise corporate, financial, commercial and legal information so questions can be answered consistently.

items.title: Clear professional responsibilities
items.html: Identify which work sits with management, the CA, legal advisers and registered issue intermediaries. Coordination is useful when those roles remain explicit.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
Rapid supports the agreed readiness review, document coordination and action tracking. We help organise the company's information and follow up on inputs needed by appointed professionals.

The proposal identifies the stages included. Rapid is not presented as the registered merchant banker, underwriter, legal certifier or exchange. Issue management and regulated responsibilities remain with appropriately appointed intermediaries.

sections.title: Information for the first discussion
sections.html: Bring the business overview, capital objective, available financial statements, shareholding structure, corporate records and details of advisers already engaged. Include major changes or unresolved matters rather than waiting for formal due diligence to surface them.

items.title: 1. Define the objective and starting position
items.html: Agree why the company is considering a listing and what readiness support is needed.

items.title: 2. Organise the evidence and gaps
items.html: Rapid coordinates a document index and action list with management and existing advisers.

items.title: 3. Support professional review
items.html: Route queries and outstanding inputs to the responsible participants.

items.title: 4. Prepare the next-stage handover
items.html: Use the readiness work to support an informed decision with the appointed issue intermediary.

sections.title: Fees and timing
sections.html: Separate readiness advisory from audit, legal, merchant-banker, exchange and other issue costs. The timetable depends on the company records and preparation required before a formal process. A fixed listing date, valuation or subscription result cannot be established from an initial enquiry.

items.title: Does Rapid guarantee an IPO?
items.html: No. Readiness support does not establish eligibility, approval or investor demand.

items.title: Must we choose Main Board or SME before speaking?
items.html: No. Start with the company and capital objective; the route is assessed using current conditions.

items.title: Can our CA remain involved?
items.html: Yes. The assignment can coordinate with the professionals already responsible for the company's records.

items.title: Does this include issue management?
items.html: Only the expressly agreed readiness and coordination stages are covered here. Regulated issue roles need the appropriate appointments.

translations.title: Mahavastu
translations.h1: Mahavastu Consultation for Your Property
translations.short_description: Discuss a traditional Vastu review of your property or layout. Rapid explains the consultation format, recommendations and practical scope.
translations.intro_html:
Review your property or layout through a structured Vastu consultation. Rapid offers this additional service for clients who want a traditional Vastu perspective on a proposed or existing home, office, shop, factory or warehouse.

Bring the space, its current use and the decisions you are considering. We explain the consultation format, recommendations and fee before the work begins.

sections.title: What can the consultation consider?
sections.html:
Rapid's published service scope includes property and direction review, layout and placement suggestions, colour guidance and a recommendation report. The discussion can concern a new plot, proposed interior arrangement or an existing occupied premises.

Vastu is a traditional belief-based approach to space. The consultation offers that perspective; it is not scientific evidence of a financial, health or business outcome.

sections.title: Which format fits the requirement?
sections.html:
Situation Discussion to have
Plan available and a focused question Whether an online review has enough information.
Existing premises with site-specific questions Whether an on-site consultation is appropriate.
Construction or interiors proposed Which decisions can still be considered before execution.
Operating factory or office How suggestions can be considered alongside practical constraints.

items.title: A defined question
items.html: Explain what you want reviewed, such as the arrangement of an office or a proposed layout, rather than relying on a vague promise to improve everything.

items.title: A record of the suggested changes
items.html: Recommendations should identify what is proposed and where, so you can discuss them with the people responsible for the property.

items.title: Practical coordination
items.html: Any suggestion affecting a working premises must be considered alongside operations, access, safety and the approved design.

sections.title: What Rapid delivers
sections.html:
The agreed consultation defines the property, questions, review format and recommendation output. Rapid explains the information needed and provides the recommendations within that scope.

Architectural, structural, fire and other technical decisions remain with the appropriately qualified professionals. A Vastu suggestion should not override a safety requirement or statutory approval.

sections.title: What to prepare
sections.html:
Bring an available floor/site plan, location, orientation information, photographs where requested, the present use of the space and the changes you are considering. Identify which areas are fixed and which can still be altered.

For an operating facility, explain machinery, circulation and other constraints so the discussion reflects the premises as used.

items.title: 1. Define the property and questions
items.html: Agree what the consultation will examine and whether online or on-site work is suitable.

items.title: 2. Review the available information
items.html: Provide the requested plan and site details; clarify any limitations in the information.

items.title: 3. Receive and discuss recommendations
items.html: Review the suggestions and identify any questions requiring clarification.

items.title: 4. Coordinate any physical changes
items.html: Before execution, take changes affecting design or safety to the responsible professionals.

sections.title: Fees and expected timing
sections.html: The fee depends on the premises, review format and agreed output. Travel or additional visits should be stated separately where applicable. The proposal should explain when the review and recommendation discussion will take place.

items.title: Can it guarantee profit or business growth?
items.html: No. Financial outcomes depend on many factors; Vastu recommendations should not be presented as proven causation.

items.title: Can a factory be reviewed without moving major equipment?
items.html: Explain the fixed constraints. The scope should be practical and should not promise that every concern has a physical remedy.

items.title: Can we use the review before construction?
items.html: Yes. Bring the proposed plan and the decisions still open, while retaining the architect's and engineers' responsibilities.

items.title: Does this replace planning advice?
items.html: No. For permission and development questions, see Land Planning.
